threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'bus stop' instead of 'the stop' like everyone else. It's a subtle shift, but it gives away your newbie status instantly.
Last week, I saw a lad on the 35 bus passionately arguing with a traffic light, insisting it was out to get him. Only in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a pigeon stealing a slice of pizza from a street performer. It was so casual, like they both knew the hustle of this city.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can grab a döner at 4 AM and find a DJ spinning techno right next door. Only in Berlin does nightlife blend seamlessly like that.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re local if they can spot a tourist trying to take an Insta pic in front of La Taqueria and chuckle as they fumble with their camera.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a saxophonist playing 'Take Five' on the 19 Polk today, mingling with the chatter. Only in SF do you get a live jazz set with your commute.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just stroll into a bar and order a 'cerveza' like it’s the same everywhere. Here, you better specify 'estrella' or 'moritz'—else you might get a blank stare.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they ask for directions to 'La Sagrada Familia' with a perfect accent, but still end up at 'La Seu' instead.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You keep trying to pay with a contactless card, but haven't realized most of the corner shops still prefer cash. Classic rookie mistake.
Caught a guy on the N35 last night, serenading the bus with opera. Must’ve been a proper late-night cabaret. Only in Brixton, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I spotted a group of elderly men playing chess on a sidewalk while a street artist painted a mural behind them—classic Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a thriving street art scene right next to a Turkish market. It's an odd yet beautiful clash of culture and creativity.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals brace for the bus delays by packing snacks and a portable charger; the newbies just stand there, bewildered by the chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a woman playing a saxophone in the middle of the street near UN Plaza as Muni buses honked around her. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the local bars where the 'old timers' debate politics over vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newcomer by their tendency to ask for a café amb llet at 3 PM; locals stick to an espresso or skip coffee altogether by then.
